kairos.title: Kairos
kairos.author: Jenny Erpenbeck
kairos.why: A love affair in 1980s East Berlin mirrors the collapse of East Germany; readers find it devastating and beautifully written.

on beauty.title: On Beauty
on beauty.author: Zadie Smith
on beauty.why: Campus novel about two feuding families; named mostly as a disliked, abandoned read.

come closer.title: Come Closer
come closer.author: Sara Gran
come closer.why: A short, pulpy tale of a woman who suspects she is being possessed; readers call it a great creepy quick read.

last and first men.title: Last and First Men
last and first men.author: Olaf Stapledon
last and first men.why: A future history of humanity across two billion years, written like a chronicle; admired for its sweeping imagination.

independent people.title: Independent People
independent people.author: Halldór Laxness
independent people.why: An Icelandic sheep farmer fights for independence in a harsh landscape; readers praise its bleak, magnificent prose.

memoirs of hadrian.title: Memoirs of Hadrian
memoirs of hadrian.author: Marguerite Yourcenar
memoirs of hadrian.why: The Roman emperor reflects on his life in a letter; a celebrated, elegant historical novel.

protector of the small.title: Protector of the Small (First Test, Page, Squire, Lady Knight)
protector of the small.author: Tamora Pierce
protector of the small.why: A girl becomes the first female knight trainee in her realm; a loved fantasy quartet with a strong heroine.

no one is talking about this.title: No One Is Talking About This
no one is talking about this.author: Patricia Lockwood
no one is talking about this.why: A woman lost in the internet is pulled back to real life by a family crisis; strange, funny and moving.

oathbringer.title: Oathbringer
oathbringer.author: Brandon Sanderson
oathbringer.why: Third Stormlight Archive book, with big revelations and battles; fans love it for its scale and character arcs.

big trouble.title: Big Trouble
big trouble.author: Dave Barry
big trouble.why: A farcical Miami caper where unrelated schemes collide; readers say this humour columnist's novel made them laugh out loud.

times arrow.title: Time's Arrow
times arrow.author: Martin Amis
times arrow.why: A man's life is narrated backwards, slowly revealing a terrible past; short and unsettling, readers say it haunts them.

rabbit.title: Rabbit: The Autobiography of Ms. Pat
rabbit.author: Patricia Williams
rabbit.why: A comedian's frank, funny memoir of a hard upbringing; readers found it gripping and finished it in days.

junky.title: Junky
junky.author: William S. Burroughs
junky.why: A raw semi-autobiographical account of heroin addiction in 1940s America, written in blunt, flat prose.

menewood.title: Menewood
menewood.author: Nicola Griffith
menewood.why: Sequel to Hild, following a seventh-century Anglo-Saxon woman through war and politics; fans love the immersive detail.

timequake.title: Timequake
timequake.author: Kurt Vonnegut
timequake.why: A time hiccup forces everyone to relive a decade; late Vonnegut, a mix of fiction and reflections.

thinking fast and slow.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
thinking fast and slow.author: Daniel Kahneman
thinking fast and slow.why: A tour of how the mind makes quick and slow decisions and where it goes wrong; a modern psychology classic.

swimming in the dark.title: Swimming in the Dark
swimming in the dark.author: Tomasz Jedrowski
swimming in the dark.why: A secret love affair between two young men in communist Poland; readers find it tender and moving.

elements.title: The Elements
elements.author: John Boyne
elements.why: Comments do not clearly discuss this book, so there is no real recommendation.

salt to the sea.title: Salt to the Sea
salt to the sea.author: Ruta Sepetys
salt to the sea.why: Four young refugees in 1945 flee toward a doomed ship; a quick, gripping and moving WWII story.

thistlefoot.title: Thistlefoot
thistlefoot.author: GennaRose Nethercott
thistlefoot.why: Two siblings inherit a living house on chicken legs that is hunted by a sinister figure; a folklore-rich Baba Yaga tale.

dracula by bram stoker.title: Dracula
dracula by bram stoker.author: Bram Stoker
dracula by bram stoker.why: The original vampire novel told through letters and diaries; readers keep returning to it for its dread.

where are you going where have you been.title: Where are you going, where have you been?
where are you going where have you been.author: Joyce Carol Oates
where are you going where have you been.why: A famous, chilling short story about a teenage girl and a menacing stranger; often cited as a favourite.

end of october.title: The End of October
end of october.author: Lawrence Wright
end of october.why: A pandemic thriller written before COVID that readers found uncannily realistic.

poor things.title: Poor things
poor things.author: Alasdair Gray
poor things.why: A Victorian tale with several unreliable narrators about a woman brought back to life; playful and inventive.

empress of salt and fortune.title: The empress of salt and fortune
empress of salt and fortune.author: Nghi Vo
empress of salt and fortune.why: A short, lyrical story of an empress's rise told through the objects her servant catalogues; a five-star pick for many.

eve.title: Eve
eve.author: Cat Bohannon
eve.why: A chapter-by-chapter history of the evolution of the female body; readers found it informative and fresh.

salt grows heavy.title: The Salt Grows Heavy
salt grows heavy.author: Cassandra Khaw
salt grows heavy.why: A dark fairy tale about a mermaid on the run with a surgeon; short, gory and richly written.

several people are typing.title: Several People Are Typing
several people are typing.author: Calvin Kasulke
several people are typing.why: An office worker gets trapped inside the company Slack; an absurd, laugh-out-loud workplace satire told in chat messages.

record of a spaceborn few.title: Record of a Spaceborn Few
record of a spaceborn few.author: Becky Chambers
record of a spaceborn few.why: Quiet, character-driven stories of ordinary lives on a generation fleet; readers love its warmth and humanity.

aristoi.title: Aristoi
aristoi.author: Walter Jon Williams
aristoi.why: A far-future society ruled by godlike minds meets a threat; admired as an underrated, idea-rich novel.

small great things.title: Small Great Things
small great things.author: Jodi Picoult
small great things.why: A Black nurse is accused after a newborn dies, in a story about racism and prejudice; an easy, popular read.

wars of light and shadow.title: The Wars of Light and Shadow
wars of light and shadow.author: Janny Wurts
wars of light and shadow.why: A sprawling, dense epic fantasy series with intricate politics; fans praise its depth despite its heavy prose.

rose madder.title: Rose Madder
rose madder.author: Stephen King
rose madder.why: A King novel of an abused wife and a magical painting, but readers here find it slow and dull.

assistant to the villain.title: Assistant to the Villain
assistant to the villain.author: Hannah Nicole Maehrer
assistant to the villain.why: A cosy, funny romance-fantasy about an assistant working for a dark lord; a light, popular comfort read.

conclave.title: Conclave
conclave.author: Robert Harris
conclave.why: Cardinals gather to elect a new pope amid intrigue and secrets; a fast, clever page-turner.

fayne.title: Fayne
fayne.author: Ann-Marie MacDonald
fayne.why: A long Victorian-era gothic adventure with a heroine and secrets; readers are eagerly reading it.

long bright river.title: Long Bright River
long bright river.author: Liz Moore
long bright river.why: A Philadelphia cop searches for her missing sister amid the opioid crisis; part mystery, part family drama.

wishing game.title: The Wishing Game
wishing game.author: Meg Shaffer
wishing game.why: A sweet whimsical romance, but the comments mostly mention it as a did-not-finish.

wild seed.title: Wild seed
wild seed.author: Octavia E. Butler
wild seed.why: Two immortals with opposing powers clash across centuries; readers can't stop thinking about it.

tartar steppe.title: The Tartar Steppe
tartar steppe.author: Dino Buzzati
tartar steppe.why: A young officer waits for an enemy at a remote fortress while life passes him by; a haunting classic about waiting.

keep.title: The Keep
keep.author: Jennifer Egan
keep.why: Two cousins renovate a castle in Europe in a gothic story with a twist; readers devour it in one sitting.

listen for the lie.title: Listen for the Lie
listen for the lie.author: Amy Tintera
listen for the lie.why: A true-crime-podcast mystery, but the comments mostly criticise the plot.

you cant win.title: You Can't Win
you cant win.author: Jack Black
you cant win.why: A burglar's 1926 memoir of crime, prison and addiction in America; a cult favourite among writers.

mirror and the light.title: The Mirror and the Light
mirror and the light.author: Hilary Mantel
mirror and the light.why: The finale of the Cromwell trilogy, covering Thomas Cromwell's final years at Henry VIII's court; praised as exquisite.

in the distance.title: In the Distance
in the distance.author: Hernán Díaz
in the distance.why: A Swedish boy crosses the American frontier alone in the 1800s; a quiet, spare reimagining of the Western.

chronoliths.title: The Chronoliths
chronoliths.author: Robert Charles Wilson
chronoliths.why: Giant monuments from the future start appearing and reshaping the world; a favourite for its central idea.

shardik.title: Shardik
shardik.author: Richard Adams
shardik.why: A hunter believes a great bear is a god and follows it into war; an unusual, harsh fantasy from the Watership Down author.

memories of ice.title: Memories of Ice
memories of ice.author: Steven Erikson
memories of ice.why: The second Malazan novel, with vast battles, magic and shifting alliances; fans consider it incredible.

family tree.title: The Family Tree
family tree.author: Sheri S. Tepper
family tree.why: Ecological fable in which a woman and a tree begin to merge; readers remember its shocking mid-book turn.

purple hibiscus.title: Purple Hibiscus
purple hibiscus.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
purple hibiscus.why: A Nigerian girl grows up under her violently religious father; a moving coming-of-age story.

carpe jugulum.title: Carpe Jugulum
carpe jugulum.author: Terry Pratchett
carpe jugulum.why: Discworld witches take on a family of modern, sun-tolerant vampires; a sharp, funny send-up of vampire stories.

before they are hanged.title: Before They Are Hanged
before they are hanged.author: Joe Abercrombie
before they are hanged.why: Middle book of The First Law, with a gritty quest and war; known for dark humour and flawed characters.

moonbound.title: Moonbound
moonbound.author: Robin Sloan
moonbound.why: In a far future, a boy meets a talking dragon in a world shaped by AI; readers like its ideas.

emperors soul.title: The Emperor's Soul
emperors soul.author: Brandon Sanderson
emperors soul.why: A forger must recreate an emperor's soul in 100 days; a short, clever fantasy novella.

loneliness of sonia and sunny.title: The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny
loneliness of sonia and sunny.author: Kiran Desai
loneliness of sonia and sunny.why: A long, sweeping novel about two Indians in love across continents; readers have mixed feelings but many praise it.

amazing maurice and his educated rodents.title: The Amazing Maurice and His Educated Rodents
amazing maurice and his educated rodents.author: Terry Pratchett
amazing maurice and his educated rodents.why: A cat and clever rats run a Pied Piper scam; a sharp, darkly funny Discworld story for younger readers.

shift.title: Shift
shift.author: Hugh Howey
shift.why: Prequel in the Silo series, showing how the underground silos came to be; a gripping dystopian page-turner.

fiasco.title: Fiasco
fiasco.author: Stanisław Lem
fiasco.why: Humans try and fail to communicate with an alien civilisation; a pessimistic, philosophical contact novel.

long earth.title: The Long Earth
long earth.author: Terry Pratchett
long earth.why: People discover they can step into endless parallel Earths; readers love the premise and exploration.

chronology of water.title: The Chronology of Water
chronology of water.author: Lidia Yuknavitch
chronology of water.why: A swimmer's raw memoir of abuse, addiction and finding herself through writing; fragmented, poetic and powerful.

to build a fire.title: To Build a Fire
to build a fire.author: Jack London
to build a fire.why: A man tries to survive a deadly cold Yukon trek; a classic survival short story.

funny story.title: Funny Story
funny story.author: Emily Henry
funny story.why: A popular romcom, but the comments find the characters unlikeable.

immortalists.title: The Immortalists
immortalists.author: Chloe Benjamin
immortalists.why: Four siblings visit a fortune teller who tells them their death dates; the novel follows how that shapes their lives.

merchanters luck.title: Merchanter's Luck
merchanters luck.author: C. J. Cherryh
merchanters luck.why: A lone trader and a starship captain meet in a space-station economy; an acclaimed entry in Alliance-Union.

sandwich.title: Sandwich
sandwich.author: Catherine Newman
sandwich.why: A family holiday on Cape Cod with a woman in menopause; warm, funny and moving.

winners.title: The Winners
winners.author: Fredrik Backman
winners.why: Backman's concluding Beartown novel about a town facing old wounds and tragedy; readers say it left them destroyed.

west with the night.title: West with the Night
west with the night.author: Beryl Markham
west with the night.why: A pioneering pilot's memoir of life in Kenya and flying; praised as brilliantly written.

people of paper.title: The People of Paper
people of paper.author: Salvador Plascencia
people of paper.why: An inventive postmodern novel with narrators fighting their author; readers call it fun and strange.

forgotten beasts of eld.title: The Forgotten Beasts of Eld
forgotten beasts of eld.author: Patricia A. McKillip
forgotten beasts of eld.why: A sorceress living with magical beasts must care for an unexpected child; a lyrical, beloved fantasy.

speak memory.title: Speak, Memory
speak memory.author: Vladimir Nabokov
speak memory.why: Nabokov's lyrical memoir of his privileged Russian childhood and exile.
